title: Internet linking
idea: VoIP carries ham voice over the internet. IRLP links repeaters, and you reach it from your radio with DTMF. EchoLink lets you get in from a computer, with no radio.

items: Voice delivered over the internet using digital techniques
Connects ham systems such as repeaters over the internet. Reach a node over the air with DTMF tones
Lets you transmit through a repeater without a radio. Register your call sign and show proof of license first
A ham station that connects other ham stations to the internet
Lets nearby transceivers reach a digital voice or data network

config.heading: Which one do you need?
config.lead: Pick what you want to do.

situations.label: Talk through a repeater from my computer, no radio
situations.title: EchoLink
situations.text: EchoLink lets a station transmit through a repeater without using a radio. Before you use it, register your call sign and provide proof of license. Any license class works, and there's no fee or training.

situations.label: Reach an internet-linked node from my radio
situations.title: IRLP, using DTMF
situations.text: IRLP connects repeaters and other ham systems over the internet. Over the air, you access a node with DTMF tones, not a password or a CTCSS tone.

situations.label: Get my digital radio onto a network from home
situations.title: A hotspot
situations.text: A digital mode hotspot lets nearby transceivers communicate with a digital voice or data network.

situations.label: Connect other hams' stations to the internet
situations.title: A gateway
situations.text: An amateur station that connects other amateur stations to the internet is a gateway.

situations.label: Carry voice over the internet
situations.title: VoIP
situations.text: Voice Over Internet Protocol delivers voice over the internet using digital techniques.

compare.how: Links repeaters over the internet. You get in from your radio with DTMF.
You can get in from a computer, with no radio. Register with proof of license.
A station that connects other hams to the internet.
Puts your nearby digital radio on a digital network.

traps.wrong: By using Continuous Tone-Coded Squelch System (CTCSS) tone codes
traps.why: CTCSS opens a repeater's squelch. IRLP nodes are accessed with DTMF tones.

traps.wrong: A set of rules specifying how to identify your station when linked over the internet to another station
traps.why: VoIP isn't an ID rule. It's how voice travels over the internet, digitally.

traps.wrong: A system for providing access to websites via amateur radio
traps.why: IRLP links radio systems such as repeaters. It isn't web access over the air.
IRLP is reached over the air with DTMF, so you need a radio. EchoLink is the one that works without one.

traps.wrong: At least a General Class license
traps.why: Any licensed ham can use EchoLink. You register your call sign and show proof of license.
The station that connects other amateur stations to the internet is called a gateway.

traps.wrong: FT8 digital communications via AFSK using a smartphone connected to the internet
traps.why: A hotspot links nearby digital radios to a digital voice or data network. It isn't an FT8 tool.
